note: Twelve items. Score each honestly - a generous score helps nobody. Most first-pass profiles land in the 30s and 40s. The weighting is deliberate: the name field, the first bio line and the pinned three are worth more than the photo, because they are what a stranger who arrived from one reel actually processes before deciding to follow. Innovation Labs edition: read 'the person' as the program/organisation, 'offer' as the program, application or event, and 'buyer' as a founder, partner or mentor deciding whether to engage.

items.full_marks: The name field (30 characters, the bold line, not the handle) carries the name plus what they do in words people search: 'Dana Ruiz | Proposal templates'. This field is indexed by Instagram search and most accounts waste it on a name alone.
items.common_fail: Just a name, or a name with an emoji.

items.full_marks: Line one names who this is for and what changes for them, in their words. Not a job title, not a list of adjectives, not three emoji separated by bars.
The rest of the 150 characters carries one piece of proof or one specific offer, and reads as sentences rather than a pipe-separated list.

Three pinned posts doing three jobs: the clearest explanation of what Innovation Labs is and who it is for, the strongest real proof (a recap with real people and outcomes approved for public use), and the current call to action (applications, next event).
items.common_fail: Nothing pinned, so the top of the grid is whatever was posted last.

items.full_marks: One destination that matches what the bio just promised. Up to five links are allowed; more than two is a menu, and a menu converts worse than a door.
items.common_fail: A link tree with eleven options, or no link at all.

items.full_marks: Four to six highlights named for what founders and partners ask: Program, Apply, Events, Stories, FAQ, Partners. Consistent IL covers. Nothing stale at the front.
The first nine covers are legible at thumbnail size and say what the account is about without a single tap. Reel covers are chosen deliberately, not left as frame one.
items.common_fail: Nine covers of a face mid-word with no text.

items.full_marks: Face fills roughly 60% of a circle that renders at about 40 pixels. Eyes visible, shot in the last two years, background not competing.
items.common_fail: A full-body shot, a logo for a personal brand, or a photo taken at arm's length in a dark room.

items.full_marks: Readable, sayable out loud, and the same handle as the other platforms. No stacked underscores or numbers standing in for letters.
items.common_fail: A handle nobody can spell after hearing it once.

items.full_marks: Professional account with a category that matches the offer, and contact buttons that work. Email that is checked, not the one from 2019.
items.common_fail: Personal account, so there are no insights and no contact button.

items.full_marks: Posted in the last seven days and replied to comments on the most recent post. An account that last posted in March reads as closed.
items.common_fail: A five-week gap, or a wall of unanswered comments.

items.full_marks: A story up right now, or at least most days. It is the difference between a profile and a person.
